title: Your First Weekend at Drexel University, Shared as Cards
description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning Drexel’s campus layout, finding practical student resources, sharing a meal, and leaving room for recreation.

cards.title: Friday: Start at Main Building
cards.subtitle: Set one dependable campus reference point
cards.notes: Begin inside only if the building is open. Notice the Great Court and the locations of Main Auditorium, Main 220 Lounge, and the galleries without assuming each space shares the same schedule.
cards.short_summary: Use Drexel’s original building to establish your bearings before exploring the rest of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel’s original Main Building contains the Great Court, Main Auditorium, Main 220 Lounge, and galleries.
cards.source_title: University City Campus Self-Guided Walking Tour
cards.access_notes: Visit during posted building hours; galleries and offices may follow narrower schedules.

cards.title: Friday: Take the Campus Photo
cards.subtitle: Mark the 33rd-and-Market landmark
cards.notes: Use the paved area around the statue for a quick group photo. Do not climb on the sculpture.
cards.short_summary: Make the dragon statue your first outdoor meeting point and photo stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Mario the Magnificent, the dragon statue at 33rd and Market streets, is an official campus photo stop and a location for student-organization and University events.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; remain on the surrounding paved area and do not climb on the artwork.

cards.title: Friday: Find the Residence-Hall Hub
cards.subtitle: Learn where campus gatherings can appear
cards.notes: Walk through without relying on a scheduled event. Note the surrounding residence halls and return only when a posted program interests you.
cards.short_summary: Use this outdoor corridor to recognize a recurring location for campus social activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Race Street Walk sits among residence halls and is used for social activities and community events such as involvement fairs.
cards.source_title: University City Campus Self-Guided Walking Tour
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus walk; scheduled programs may alter circulation.

cards.title: Friday: Share an Easy Campus Dinner
cards.subtitle: Keep the first meal logistically simple
cards.notes: Choose among the available stations and check current dining hours, accepted payment methods, and meal-plan rules before going.
cards.short_summary: Pause the orientation loop for a meal at Drexel’s all-you-care-to-eat dining location.
cards.evidence_claim: Urban Eatery is Drexel’s all-you-care-to-eat dining location and contains seven stations, including vegetarian- and vegan-friendly choices.
cards.access_notes: Check current Campus Dining hours and payment rules; the cited page does not establish today’s schedule.

cards.title: Friday: Locate the After-Hours Study Base
cards.subtitle: Know where the chargers and whiteboards are
cards.notes: Identify the 33rd-and-Ludlow entrance before you need it. Bring your Dragon Card if returning after Hagerty Library closes.
cards.short_summary: End Friday by learning the practical layout of Drexel’s round-the-clock study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dragons’ Learning Den provides 24-hour access to seating, charging kiosks, whiteboards, restrooms, and vending machines.
cards.access_notes: Drexel community members use the 33rd-and-Ludlow doors and scan a Dragon Card after the main library closes.

cards.title: Saturday: Trace the Campus Spine
cards.subtitle: Connect yesterday’s landmarks on foot
cards.notes: Use the walk as an unhurried daytime orientation loop. Posted events may temporarily change how portions of the space are used.
cards.short_summary: Start Saturday outside by connecting several major student destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: Lancaster Walk connects the DAC, Rush Building, and other student destinations and is used for community activities and relaxation.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus route; check posted notices for events or temporary closures.

cards.title: Saturday: Map the Student-Support Offices
cards.subtitle: Learn where to return when services are open
cards.notes: This is a location-finding stop, not a promise that every office will be operating on the weekend. Record the offices relevant to you and consult their individual schedules later.
cards.short_summary: Find several student-life resources clustered in one campus building.
cards.evidence_claim: Rush Building houses the Center for Black Culture, Student Center for Diversity and Inclusion, Student Organization Resource Center, and Mario’s Market food pantry.
cards.access_notes: Building access and the schedules and eligibility rules of individual offices vary; verify before seeking service.

cards.title: Saturday: Try an Active Break
cards.subtitle: Inspect the recreation options before choosing one
cards.notes: Pick an activity appropriate to your experience and follow facility instructions. Verify eligibility, equipment requirements, and current-day hours before entering.
cards.short_summary: Use the recreation stop to identify which indoor activities might fit a future weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel Recreation Center includes fitness floors, an elevated track, courts, a climbing wall, and exercise rooms.
cards.access_notes: Eligibility and current-day hours should be checked before visiting; individual facilities may have additional rules.

cards.title: Saturday: Leave Room for an Outdoor Meetup
cards.subtitle: Use open space without requiring a formal event
cards.notes: Bring a simple activity or meet a new classmate there. Organized or exclusive use may require University approval.
cards.short_summary: Close Saturday with flexible time in a green space shared with the surrounding community.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel Park is a 2.5-acre green space serving both the University and Powelton Village communities and intended for recreation and relaxation.
cards.access_notes: Shared outdoor green space; organized activities may require approval, and scheduled uses can occupy part of the park.

cards.title: Sunday: Finish with a Self-Guided Art Walk
cards.subtitle: Revisit campus through its outdoor landmarks
cards.notes: Build a short route around the works that interest you and remain in public campus areas. This activity does not depend on gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: End the weekend by linking familiar paths through outdoor sculptures and landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel documents an outdoor campus-art route that includes the Drexel Clock, Anthony J. Drexel statue, Mario the Magnificent, and George Rickey’s kinetic sculpture.
cards.source_title: Hidden Treasures: Drexel’s Outdoor Public Art
cards.access_notes: The documented works are outdoors across campus; remain in public areas and observe posted restrictions.

warnings: Weekend building, office, dining, and recreation schedules can change; verify current access before relying on an indoor stop.
Free status covers the described place or activity only; optional food, equipment, transit, and separately ticketed programming are not included.
